1. (Currently amended) A method of using a finger palette to transfer cosmetics from a container to a destination, comprising:
a. the finger palette including:
i. a ring portion that is securable to a finger; and
ii. a surface portion secured to the ring portion, the surface portion being at least substantially smooth to allow a user to spread or blend cosmetic product on the surface portion;
b. the method including the steps of:
i. securing the finger palette to a finger;
ii. depositing a cosmetic product onto the surface portion of the finger palette __using an applicator tool__; and
iii. transferring the cosmetic product from the surface portion of the finger palette to a destination __using a brush or sponge applicator__.

4. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein:
a. a first quantity of the cosmetic product is deposited onto the surface portion; and
b. a second quantity of the cosmetic product is transferred from the surface portion to the destination, the second quantity being smaller than the first quantity, __wherein the cosmetic product remaining on the surface portion after transfer is intentionally retained for blending with an additional cosmetic product__.

5. (Original)

6. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein the surface portion is at least substantially without protrusions extending therefrom __and is configured to allow uninterrupted scraping motion of an applicator across the entire surface portion__.

7. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein the surface portion is at least substantially planar __and extends outwardly from a surface center to an outer perimeter without any recessed areas or trapping features__.

11. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein the finger palette is secured to the finger by passing the finger through the ring portion __such that the ring portion is removably and replaceably securable to the finger__.

2. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 further including the step of removing the cosmetic product from the container __using a dedicated removal instrument__ before depositing the cosmetic product onto the surface portion of the finger palette.

12. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein:
a. the cosmetic product is a first cosmetic product; and
b. the method further includes the step of depositing a second cosmetic product onto the surface portion of the finger palette __in a non-overlapping segment from the first cosmetic product__.

13. (Currently amended) The method of claim 12 wherein:
a. the first cosmetic product is deposited on a first segment of the surface portion; and
b. the second cosmetic product is deposited on a non-overlapping second segment of the surface portion __such that the first and second cosmetic products remain visually distinct prior to blending__.

14. (Currently amended) The method of claim 12 further including the step of blending the first cosmetic product with the second cosmetic product on the surface portion to obtain a blended cosmetic product __using a blending instrument separate from the removal instruments__.

15. (Original)

18. (Currently amended) A method of using a finger palette to transfer cosmetics from a container to a work surface, comprising:
a. the finger palette including:
i. a ring portion configured to be removably and replaceably securable to a finger; and
ii. a surface portion secured to the ring portion, the surface portion extending outwardly from a surface center to an outer perimeter, wherein the surface portion is at least substantially smooth so as to allow a user to scrape an applicator past the surface center in an uninterrupted motion while spreading or blending cosmetic product over the entirety of the surface portion;
b. the method including the steps of:
i. securing the finger palette to a finger by passing the finger through the ring portion;
ii. dispensing cosmetic product from a cosmetics container __using a first dedicated dispensing instrument__ and placing a first quantity of the dispensed cosmetic product onto the surface portion of the finger palette;
iii. removing cosmetic product from the surface portion of the finger palette __using a second dedicated removal instrument__; and
iv. applying a second quantity of the removed cosmetic product to a destination, the second quantity being smaller than the first quantity, __wherein the cosmetic product remaining on the surface portion is intentionally retained for subsequent blending or application__.

20. (Currently amended) The method of claim 18 wherein:
a. the cosmetic product is dispensed from the cosmetics container using a first instrument;
b. the cosmetic product is removed from the surface portion using a second instrument; and
c. the removed cosmetic product is applied to the destination using the second instrument __or a third instrument, and further including the steps of: i. dispensing a second cosmetic product from a second cosmetics container and placing a third quantity of the dispensed second cosmetic product onto the surface portion of the finger palette in a non-overlapping segment from the first cosmetic product; and ii. blending the first cosmetic product on the surface portion with the second cosmetic product on the surface portion to obtain a blended cosmetic product, wherein the cosmetic product applied to the destination is the blended cosmetic product__.
